caption:
Your factory sent a certificate. Whose name is on it as the certifier?
A passing lab report won't fix what the certificate itself is missing.
On imports, the certifier is usually the importer of record.
The cert also needs the certifier's full address, email and phone, plus when and where it was made, among other fields.
Want a free gap list? Comment M&Z and we'll DM you the link.
#amazonseller #cpsc #productcompliance #importing #privatelabel

sources.claim: On imports, the importer is (absent a specific rule saying otherwise) the party that must issue the certificate, so the importer, not the factory, is usually the one named as certifier.
sources.used_in: Scene 2 compare (headline 'Who's named as certifier?', Certifier: Factory vs Should be: Importer); VO2 'The certifier? The factory. On imports, it's usually the importer.'; Scene 4 item 'Certifier named / the factory' (ok:false); caption line 3
sources.section: 16 CFR 1110.7 Who must certify finished products, (a) Imports (current eCFR, Title 16 up to date as of 2026-10-19; section last amended 2026-07-08 by 90 FR 1843, Jan. 8, 2025, the eFiling rule)
sources.quote: Except as otherwise provided in a specific rule, ban, standard, or regulation enforced by CPSC, for a finished product manufactured outside of the United States that must be accompanied by a certificate as set forth in § 1110.5, the importer, as defined in this part, is the finished product certifier that must issue a finished product certificate that meets the requirements of this part.

sources.claim: In this rule 'importer' means the importer of record (supports the scenario framing 'Say the seller is the importer of record' and caption 'importer of record').
sources.used_in: Scene 2 note 'Say the seller is the importer of record.'; caption line 3
sources.section: 16 CFR 1110.3 Definitions, (b), definition of 'Importer' (current eCFR, Title 16 up to date as of 2026-10-19; section last amended 2026-07-08 by 90 FR 1843, Jan. 8, 2025, the eFiling rule)
sources.quote: Importer, for the purposes of this part, means the Importer of Record (IOR) eligible to make entry for imported finished products under the Tariff Act of 1930

sources.claim: The certificate must identify the certifier with name, street address, city, state or province, country, email and phone, so a name alone is not enough.
sources.used_in: Scene 3 pair (headline 'A name alone isn't enough.', note 'Plus street, city, state, country, email and phone.', The gap: Name only / The fix: Full contact); VO3 'A name isn't enough. Address, email and phone, too.'; Scene 4 item 'Certifier contact / name only' (ok:false); caption line 4
sources.section: 16 CFR 1110.11 Certificate content, (a) Content requirements ('Each finished product certificate must:'), (a)(3) (current eCFR, Title 16 up to date as of 2026-10-19; section last amended 2026-07-08 by 90 FR 1843, Jan. 8, 2025, the eFiling rule)
sources.quote: (3) Identify the finished product certifier that is certifying compliance of the finished product(s), as set forth in § 1110.7, including the party's name, street address, city, state or province, country or administrative region, electronic mail (email) address, and telephone number.

sources.claim: The certificate must state when (month and year at a minimum) and where the product was made.
sources.used_in: Scene 4 note 'Required too: when and where it was made.' and item 'Made: month/year / missing' (ok:false); VO4 'Plus when it was made.'; caption line 4
sources.section: 16 CFR 1110.11 Certificate content, (a) Content requirements ('Each finished product certificate must:'), (a)(5) (current eCFR, Title 16 up to date as of 2026-10-19; section last amended 2026-07-08 by 90 FR 1843, Jan. 8, 2025, the eFiling rule)
sources.quote: (5) Provide the date (month and year, at a minimum) and place (including a manufacturer name, street address, city, state or province, country or administrative region, email address, and telephone number) where the finished product(s) were manufactured, produced, or assembled.

sources.claim: These content rules apply to every finished product certificate (CPC and GCC), so the reel names neither type and cannot mix them up.

sources.section: 16 CFR 1110.3 Definitions, (b), definition of 'Finished product certificate' (current eCFR, Title 16 up to date as of 2026-10-19; section last amended 2026-07-08 by 90 FR 1843, Jan. 8, 2025, the eFiling rule)
sources.quote: Finished product certificate means a certificate of compliance for a finished product, as defined in this section, that is required by § 1110.5. There are two types of finished product certificates: Children's Product Certificates (CPCs) and General Certificates of Conformity (GCCs).

Certificate didn't.'; VO5 now says the full CTA; scene 2 raised 4.4 -> 4.6 s for voice margin. No new claims were added.
3) Timing: total 23.9 s, only 0.1 s under the 24 s cap. Real TTS spare per scene: 1.33 / 0.52 / 0.42 / 0.92 / 1.45 s. If you record the lines yourself and a scene runs long, do NOT let voice.py --fit push the total past 24 s; instead drop ', link in bio' from VO5 (URL is on screen; scene 5 can then go to 5.1 s, freeing 1.1 s). Never cut a claim line.
4) Still times: with these durations the standard stills 0.5/4/9/15/20 skip scene 3 (pair, 9.7-13.7 s). Add 12 (and 17 for the full checklist). Glance at the compare scene: the template paints BOTH values red-highlighted (diff highlight), including the correct 'Importer' side; the blue bar and 'Should be' label carry the meaning. That is template behavior, not a content issue, but check you are happy with it.
5) 'Should be: Importer' has no hedge on screen and is accurate only inside the scenario note 'Say the seller is the importer of record.' Keep that note. The rule starts 'Except as otherwise provided in a specific rule...', a customs broker that is IOR may name the owner/purchaser/consignee, and a factory can itself be IOR. Hence 'usually' in VO2 and caption line 3.
6) Never say or reply 'the factory can't be on the cert'. 1110.11(a)(5) requires the manufacturer's name and address as the place of manufacture. The reel only says who is NAMED AS CERTIFIER. For DMs only (not used in the reel or caption, since it is outside the verified claim set): 1110.15 says a certifier 'may rely on another party to enter data into the Product Registry or to certify finished products on their behalf' but 'remains legally responsible' (verbatim in the fresh eCFR fetch). No legal verdicts in DMs.
7) The field lists are partial on purpose. 1110.11(a) also requires the product identifier, every applicable rule, the records-keeper contact, the test date and place, and the attestation. The caption says 'among other fields'; keep it that way in replies.
8) No CPC or GCC is named, which is correct because 1110.11(a) covers both. If anyone asks, KID-24-BLUE implies a children's product, which would be a CPC. Never call it a GCC.
9) Tracking vs bio: the reel and caption say 'link in bio', but the playbook bio link is the Finder (?src=ig_bio), not the gap list. Clicks would land on the Finder and count as ig_bio. Decide whether to point the bio link (or a story link sticker) to https://mzconsulting.agency/?src=ig_20261021_gap#contact for this reel's run; otherwise this reel's gap-list requests won't be attributable.
10) Sources: only current eCFR text (post-eFiling numbering, 90 FR 1843). The human eCFR URLs redirected curl to eCFR's bot gate, so I verified the text through the versioner API. Please open the 3 section links in a browser once. Do not cite the cpsc.gov CPC FAQ; it predates the eFiling rules.
